summary: Broome County, NY tower on Ingraham Hill beside WNBF transmitters; opened 1950 (press still building mid-1951); sold early 1970s; taken down Oct 2016; site posted private.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40 steel tower, 80 ft (Starr list); 1950 press: 91 ft overall, cab 80 ft to platform; plans called for a glass-enclosed cab and three-room observer cabin
facts.status_note: Taken down in October 2016 per the FFLA New York annual report for 2016; the 2011 Starr list still had it standing
facts.agency: New York State Conservation Department (the Starr list files it under NYS-DEC)

access.note: Posted private land and closed to the public, per the 2011 Starr list. The 1950 press names WNBF-TV and Clark Associates, Inc. as owners.

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb; the 2011 list says the site is posted private land

events.note: Starr list: opened and tower year 1950, Aermotor LS-40, 80 ft. Press: lease approved Nov 1950, work set to start Nov 1950, still being completed July 1951.
Taken down in October 2016 (annual report); the November 2016 newsletter says it came down.

corrections.why: The Starr list gives 80 ft and the November 2016 newsletter says an 80 foot tower. 27.4 m is 90 ft, the figure from the 1950 plan; the later press says 91 ft overall with 80 ft to the platform.
The 2011 Starr list gives 'Private land - No public access' for the site.
The 2016 annual report says the tower was taken down in October; the newsletter says it came down. Neither source gives a cause, so 'destroyed' goes beyond the evidence.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Starr list gives 1950 for both opened and tower. The press shows a lease in November 1950 and the tower still being finished in July 1951. The story uses 1950 and reports the 1951 report.
The Starr list and the 2016 newsletter say 80 ft. The 1950 press says 91 ft overall with 80 ft to the platform. The story gives both.
The November 1950 press names WNBF-TV as owner of the tower site in one report and Clark Associates, Inc. as owner in another. The story reports both and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: Built year and height rest on the Starr list and 1950-51 press clippings, which disagree on dates and height; both are reported in the story. Removal in October 2016 is documented by two FFLA newsletters, so it is high confidence. No source describes what remains on the hill now. Facebook group posts seen only in search results (not fetched) say the steel tower was pulled over in 2016; not used. The NHLR pictorial PDF (nhlr.org/media/2972/) has a 1950 photo caption of the tower under construction, but no license was found, so no photo was added. The Starr list says the tower was sold in the early 1970s; no exact year is given, so no event was added for it. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the glass-enclosed cab and three-room cabin were planned in 1950, not confirmed as built, and the story now says so. The 2011 list's private-land wording is now quoted in full.
